title: Online defamation by anonymous accounts - how to identify and sue them
p1:
Someone posts false accusations about you online and disappears behind a fake profile. Can you really find them?

Many people assume anonymous accounts cannot be held responsible. That is one of the biggest myths about online defamation.
p2: An anonymous username does not make a person invisible. In many cases, digital trails such as account details, IP records, email information, and platform data can help identify the person behind the account through the proper legal process.
p3:
The key step is preserving evidence before it disappears. Save screenshots, URLs, dates, and any details connected to the account. A legal notice or court process may then be used to request information from platforms and internet service providers.

The surprising part? Deleting a post does not always erase the evidence. Digital records may still exist.

If someone attacks your reputation online, acting quickly can make a major difference.
conclusion: Do you think anonymous social media accounts should have the same legal responsibility as identified users? Share your view.
